newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends firmer, May still shy of 900 stg.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends firmer, May still shy of 900 stg.

text.p: London cocoa futures reached higher on speculative short covering on Thursday although benchmark prices stayed shy of the 900 stg mark.
Traders said an initial lift was provided by sterling's weakness against other European currencies.
Follow-through buying came as shorts sought cover and rolled positions against tightening spreads before the expiry of the March position. There was also some industry interest, traders said.
The spot March/May spread was trading at 20 stg compared to 27 stg on Wednesday.
A lot of the day's 10,682 lots of turnover consisted of price fixation against the nearbys and switches. Origins were said to be less active compared to previous days, traders said.
The May contract ended seven stg higher at 893 stg after touching 898 stg, but the day's biggest winner was spot March with a 11-stg gain at 876 stg.
The technical outlook has improved after the market's performance in the last two days and some traders say the rally is likely to continue.
"After yesterday's level it looks to me like it could reach higher. It wants to try to test above 900, maybe tomorrow," said one.

But the latest Ghana purchases failed to stir any reaction with traders saying the 8,687 tonnes of cocoa purchased in the 17th week of the 1996/97 campaign, from 12,365 the week before, was in line with expectations of a seasonal drop.
Cumulative purchases by the end of February 8 were 281,558 tonnes.
In other news, the Economist Intelligence Unit (EIU) forecast the Ivorian 1996/97 crop at 980,000 tonnes, down from an estimated 1.2 million in the previous season.
Total output was seen lower at 2.6 million tonnes, resulting in a supply shortfall of 145,000 tonnes compared with a surplus of 133,000 last season.
